about: Provenance for the five canonical transition anchors.
These frames are art direction, not shipped assets: nothing in src/ loads
them and Vite never emits them. What they do is fix the stretch of the
journey from SHAY's forecourt out to contact, and every dimension of the
route's geometry in src/journey/scene.ts is measured off them. That is why
they need a record: a number in the world that came off a picture is only
as trustworthy as the picture still being the one it was measured from.
`npm run assets:verify` re-hashes every file here and fails on a mismatch,
a missing file, or a file in the directory that this manifest does not
list. Replacing an anchor is a decision about the journey — see the
'Replacing one' section of README.md — and it means editing this file by
hand. Nothing rewrites it: a manifest a script can update is a manifest
that agrees with whatever is on disk.
`generator` is null on all five and stays null. They arrived as a bare
upload with no model, prompt or settings recorded, and inventing a
plausible source would be worse than saying so. What is recorded instead
is exactly what can be checked: who committed them, when, and under which
sha. They cannot be regenerated; they can be verified.

anchors.role: SHAY exit → the exterior route toward TIMEMATIC.
measuredInto: ROUTE.facade.z / .x — TIMEMATIC's front reads at ~0.22 of the frame from across the plaza, which is what puts the building at -19900 and makes the plaza long enough to be crossed.
ROUTE.plaza — the run of ground the route comes down onto.

source.note: Committed as a bare binary upload with no model, prompt or settings recorded. Not reproducible; verify by hash.

anchors.role: The final TIMEMATIC portfolio viewing position. The camera stops here while the project is presented.
measuredInto: WORK_READS = 0.273 — the share of frame width the work fills at the stop, which is what fixes the stop's distance per viewport.
ROUTE.hall.x and ROUTE.wall.z — the hall's walls reach the display's edges at the stop, giving a 4320-wide hall at depth -2000.
ROUTE.display — 1180 wide, and 707 tall from the measured 1.67 aspect.

measuredInto: npm run measure:yaw — this is the test frame for whether the route's camera turns. Nothing in ROUTE is solved from it yet: the corridor is a later act.
